name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with R+23 partisan lean
Incumbent Rick Crawford running with a large cash advantage
Democrat Terri Green raised only $65k with $12k on hand
model.rationale: Crawford is a well-funded incumbent in a district that leans Republican by 23 points, while Green has raised almost nothing and has minimal cash on hand. Markets price Crawford near certain, and no polling or expert ratings suggest any reason to move off the fundamentals.
model.watch: A surprise wave election or major scandal could narrow the margin, but nothing in the current evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Crawford seeks another term in this deeply Republican northeast Arkansas district, which has a 23-point Republican lean. He enters the general election with over $1 million on hand after raising more than $940,000. Democrat Terri Green has raised only about $65,000 and had under $12,000 in cash as of the latest filings, leaving her badly outmatched financially. A Libertarian candidate, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets give Crawford roughly a 98% chance of winning. The combination of the district's partisan lean, Crawford's incumbency advantage, and his overwhelming financial edge makes this a safe Republican seat, with the main question being the size of the margin rather than the outcome.
